articles.title: Keep Business Data on Your Own Machine: A Local-First Desktop Agent Architecture
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm Peijian Xu, CTO at aiFetchly. I work on aiFetchly, the open-source desktop agent described below, so this is a team perspective — not an independent review. Most business AI agents wor…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm Peijian Xu, CTO at aiFetchly. I work on aiFetchly, the open-source desktop agent described below, so this is a team perspective — not an independent review. The problem with sending everything to the cloud Most business AI agents work the same way: you upload documents, emails and customer notes to someone else's server, and hope the answers that come back are grounded in your own material. That is convenient, but it creates three practical problems for a small business: You lose track of where your data lives. Contracts, price lists and customer history end up scattered across SaaS tools. Answers drift from your source material. When the agent cannot see your own notes, it fills gaps with generic text. Routine work still needs a human in the loop.

articles.title: Next.js Bundling a wasm Package Breaks Only in Production
articles.excerpt: Conclusion An npm package that loads a wasm file breaks when included in the standard Next.js bundle. If the package resolves its wasm by relative path internally, bundling changes what that path is r…
articles.body: Conclusion An npm package that loads a wasm file breaks when included in the standard Next.js bundle. If the package resolves its wasm by relative path internally, bundling changes what that path is relative to, and it fails at runtime with a type error. The fix is to exclude the package from bundling with serverExternalPackages and to explicitly include the wasm itself in the deployment with outputFileTracingIncludes — both, not one. Symptom Requests issuing a document PDF return 502 in production only The same failure reproduces locally under next build && next start (production build mode) The log shows this type error TypeError: The "path" argument must be of type string … Received type number A type error where a string path should be passed.

articles.title: Why Your PC Randomly Restarts: A Practical Windows Crash Forensics Guide
articles.excerpt: A powerful PC can restart without warning even when temperatures appear normal and the hardware is relatively new. The difficult part is not finding an error in Event Viewer. It is establishing what t…
articles.body: A powerful PC can restart without warning even when temperatures appear normal and the hardware is relatively new. The difficult part is not finding an error in Event Viewer. It is establishing what the error actually proves — and what it does not. This guide presents an evidence-first workflow for investigating unexpected restarts in Windows 10 and 11. Kernel-Power 41 is an observation, not a diagnosis When Windows detects that the preceding shutdown was not clean, it may log Kernel-Power Event ID 41 during startup. Its timestamp can therefore be later than the actual failure. An unexpected restart can follow a stop error, loss of power, a forced shutdown or another failure that prevents a normal shutdown.

articles.title: Why macOS Is My Second Favourite OS as a Linux Developer
articles.excerpt: Linux is my favourite operating system. I run openSUSE with KDE Plasma on my desktop, and much of my homelab runs on Linux. However, I also genuinely enjoy using macOS. What's interesting is that many…
articles.body: Linux is my favourite operating system. I run openSUSE with KDE Plasma on my desktop, and much of my homelab runs on Linux. However, I also genuinely enjoy using macOS. What's interesting is that many of the reasons I like macOS are the same reasons I like Linux. Others are things I wish Linux did a little better. As a software developer, Linux enthusiast and electronic music producer, here's why macOS is my second favourite operating system. A Familiar Unix Foundation Although macOS looks quite different from most Linux desktop environments, the two operating systems share a lot of concepts under the hood. macOS is built on Darwin, which incorporates the XNU kernel and draws from Mach and BSD technologies.

articles.excerpt: The Aladdin sequel The Return of Jafar is often derided as a bad, cheap sequel which started Disney's direct-to-video sequel trend, but I love it
articles.body: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
